sec: Malaria: clinical features, complications, species characteristics

items.q: Malaria — match the clinical group to its content — 1) Symptoms 2) Signs 3) Complication mechanism … A) Extreme fatigue B) Organ ischaemia C) Tachypnoea, tachycardia, splenomegaly
items.exp: 'clinical features : · Extreme fatigue'; 'Tachypnea / tachycardia / splenomegaly'; 'complication : Organ ischemia'. (Book p1059)

items.q: What mechanism is printed for the complications of falciparum malaria?
opts: Cyto-adherence, rosetting and agglutination of RBCs

items.q: Which organ is printed as the major site of RBC trapping?
items.exp: '· major organ involved in trapping RBCs : Spleen'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Which investigation is printed for malaria on this page?
Species characteristics — match — 1) P. falciparum 2) P. vivax 3) P. ovale 4) P. malariae … A) Reticulocytes, up to 2 weeks old B) Reticulocytes C) Older cells D) Younger cells
items.exp: 'Red cell preference : Younger cells (falciparum); Reticulocytes and cells up to 2 weeks old (vivax); Reticulocytes (ovale); Older cells (malariae)'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Duration of the erythrocytic cycle printed for P. falciparum and P. vivax?
Which species is printed with a 72-hour erythrocytic cycle?
items.exp: 'Duration of erythrocytic cycle (Hours) : … P. malariae 72'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Pigment colour — match — 1) P. falciparum 2) P. vivax 3) P. ovale 4) P. malariae … A) Yellow-brown B) Dark-brown C) Brown-black D) Black
items.exp: 'Pigment color : Black (falciparum), Yellow-brown (vivax), Dark-brown (ovale), Brown-black (malariae)'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Relapses — match the species to its ability — 1) P. vivax 2) P. ovale 3) P. falciparum 4) P. malariae … A) Yes B) Yes C) No D) No
items.exp: 'Ability to cause relapses : No (falciparum), Yes (vivax), Yes (ovale), No (malariae)'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Uncomplicated versus complicated — match — 1) Uncomplicated 2) Complicated … A) Due to P. falciparum, with anaemia, cerebral malaria, hypoglycaemia, shock, haemoglobinuria and jaundice B) Due to P. falciparum or P. vivax, with fever and chills, fatigue, diaphoresis and mild myalgia
items.exp: 'Uncomplicated malaria : (d/t P. falciparum / P. vivax) — Fever with chills / fatigue / diaphoresis, Tachypnea / tachycardia / splenomegaly, myalgia (Not severe)'; 'Complicated malaria : (d/t P. falciparum) — Anemia, Cerebral malaria, Hypoglycemia, Hypotension/shock, Hemoglobinuria (black water fever), Jaundice'. (Book p1059)

items.q: Which colour name is given to the haemoglobinuria of complicated malaria?
Which is NOT printed among the features of complicated malaria?
items.exp: Printed: anaemia, cerebral malaria (convulsions, seizures), hypoglycaemia, hypotension/shock, haemoglobinuria and jaundice. (Book p1059)

items.q: A patient with falciparum malaria has seizures and hypoglycaemia. Which group and species does the page assign this to?
opts: Complicated malaria due to P. falciparum
Uncomplicated malaria due to P. vivax
items.exp: Cerebral malaria with convulsions, seizures and hypoglycaemia is listed under 'Complicated malaria : (d/t P. falciparum)'. (Book p1059)
